summary: Distributed MinIO is operational across node1-node4 on the dedicated 10.100.104.0/24 network. TLS S3 listens on port 9000, and node1 provides the protected `mc` alias `minio`.
actions_performed: Configured four MinIO members with persistent data volumes, node-specific TLS certificates, shared authentication, and automatic service restart.
Created private bucket `infra-data` with `proof.txt` containing exactly `distributed-storage-ready`.
Stopped node4 and verified reads and writes continued with three members.
Restored node4 and verified automatic rejoin and healing of data written during its outage.

evidence.summary: Every member is active, enabled, configured with four distributed endpoints, mounted storage, restart=always, and CA-validated TLS health 200 on port 9000.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated S3 bucket and required object
evidence.summary: Anonymous HTTPS access returns 403, while authenticated retrieval returns `distributed-storage-ready`; the final cluster reports one bucket, three objects, and four online drives.
Node1 has `/usr/local/bin/mc`, a mode-600 alias configuration, and successfully reports all four servers and EC:2 status.

evidence.requirement: Read/write availability and automatic recovery with one member unavailable
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline showed four drives; node4 was stopped with no listener; the degraded cluster remained healthy and read/wrote data with three drives; node4 was restored, rejoined 4/4 automatically, served the outage-time object, accepted another write, and its local volume contained all current objects.
